paper_title: Narrative Media Framing in Political Discourse
caption: Distribution of articles across media outlets
model_annotation: This pie chart illustrates the distribution of articles across various media outlets, displaying a total of 18 distinct slices. The chart does not utilize a separate legend; instead, category labels are positioned directly outside the perimeter of the pie, while numerical values representing the proportions are placed centrally inside each corresponding slice. There are no visually emphasized segments, such as exploded or offset slices. Visually, the segments are arranged in a generally descending order of size moving counter-clockwise from the right side, with the exception of the "Other" category, which is positioned at the end of the sequence. The largest individual named outlet is Breitbart, depicted in blue with a value of 14. Continuing counter-clockwise, the slices include Drudge Report in orange (8), The Daily Caller in green (8), The Huffington Post in red (7), NPR in purple (6), Vox in brown (6), The Guardian in pink (5), BBC in gray (5), and RT in olive green (4). The subsequent eight slices each display a value of 3 and include Daily Kos in cyan, National Review in blue, Daily Mail in orange, Red State in green, Fox News in red, CNN in purple, PoliticusUSA in brown, and Shareblue in pink. Finally, completing the circle clockwise from Breitbart is the "Other" category, shown in gray with a value of 13.
